steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Class in "Jekyll and Hyde": Jekyll is respectable middle-class professional; Hyde represents the underclass he secretly joins. Class boundaries are both rigid and permeable. | Effect on Structure: Dickens's novels have cliffhangers at chapter ends because they were originally published in parts. Each installment needed to keep readers hooked. | AO3 Context Strategy: For the 19th century novel question, AO3 is worth 25% of marks (typically 8 out of 30 marks). Spend roughly 5-7 minutes of a 45-minute response on embedding context. Never bolt context on at the end — weave it into your argument. Examiners reward contextual points that illuminate the text, not historical facts listed for their own sake. A Grade 9 response treats context as the lens through which the text's meaning becomes clear

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: How did the Industrial Revolution affect Victorian literature? | What was the Victorian "crisis of faith"? | Why were Victorians fascinated by Gothic horror?
